pages.title: Home
pages.summary: Ze turns a Linux server into a programmable network device. It speaks BGP, manages interfaces, programs the FIB, and exposes one config tree over five surfaces (CLI, Web UI, Looking Glass, MCP...

pages.title: About
pages.summary: This section is the starting point if you have never heard of Ze, or if you have and want to know what is actually inside it.

pages.title: What is Ze
pages.summary: Ze turns a Linux server into a programmable network device.

pages.title: Why Ze
pages.summary: This is the long version of "what is this for, should I care".

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: This page is the mental model.

pages.title: History
pages.summary: Where Ze came from, and how it got to where it is now.

pages.title: Status
pages.summary: Ze is in early active development.

pages.summary: This section takes you from an empty Linux box to a Ze daemon with its first BGP peer up.

pages.title: Install
pages.summary: You build Ze from source.

pages.title: Docker
pages.summary: Run Ze in a Docker container for evaluation, lab testing, or lightweight deployments where you don't need interface configuration or kernel-level features (VPP, L2TP, nftables).

pages.title: netlab
pages.summary: netlab builds a lab from a short YAML topology and starts each node under containerlab.

pages.title: Appliance
pages.summary: Ze ships a bootable VM appliance image: a minimal Linux system built with gokrazy that runs Ze as its only application.

pages.title: Quick Start
pages.summary: You have a built ze binary.

pages.title: ExaBGP Migration
pages.summary: This is the first page to read if you already run ExaBGP.

pages.title: CLI Tour
pages.summary: The Ze CLI is a network-OS shell, not a Unix CLI bolted on top of a daemon.

pages.title: Web UI Tour
pages.summary: The web UI is the same engine as the CLI with a different surface on top.

pages.title: Configuration
pages.summary: This is the configuration section.

pages.title: Overview
pages.summary: Configuration in Ze is one tree, validated by one set of YANG schemas, edited from any of the five operator surfaces (CLI, web UI, Looking Glass, MCP, REST API), committed atomically, and rolled back...

pages.title: YANG Model
pages.summary: Every field in Ze comes from a YANG schema.

pages.title: Editor Workflow
pages.summary: The config editor is the piece of Ze that turns "edit a text file and hope" into the network-OS workflow operators actually expect.

pages.title: Archive and Rollback
pages.summary: Every committed configuration in Ze is kept.

pages.title: System
pages.summary: The system { } block carries the identity of the Ze instance and the global settings that do not belong to a specific subsystem.

pages.title: Interfaces
pages.summary: Ze manages Linux network interfaces through the iface component, backed by pure netlink.

pages.title: VRRP
pages.summary: VRRP gives a LAN a gateway address that survives the loss of the router holding it.

pages.title: BFD
pages.summary: Ze includes a full BFD implementation (RFC 5880/5881/5882/5883) as a plugin.

pages.title: FIB
pages.summary: The FIB pipeline in Ze takes BGP best-path output and programs the forwarding table.

pages.title: OSPF
pages.summary: Ze includes an experimental native OSPF engine under the ospf config root.

pages.title: IS-IS
pages.summary: Ze implements IS-IS (Intermediate System to Intermediate System, ISO/IEC 10589 as updated by RFC 1195 / RFC 5305 / RFC 5308 / RFC 5301) as a native link-state interior gateway protocol that runs...

pages.title: MPLS / LDP / RSVP-TE
pages.summary: Ze can act as a Linux MPLS label-switching router (LSR).

pages.title: RSVP-TE
pages.summary: RSVP-TE (RFC 3209, on top of RFC 2205 RSVP) signals explicitly-routed MPLS LSP tunnels with bandwidth reservation.

pages.title: SRv6
pages.summary: SRv6 (Segment Routing over IPv6) Prefix-SID support (RFC 8669, RFC 9252).

pages.title: Static Routes
pages.summary: Ze supports static routes with ECMP, weighted load balancing, BFD-tracked failover, blackhole, and reject.

pages.title: Policy Routing
pages.summary: Ze supports policy-based routing (PBR) to steer traffic through alternate routing tables or next-hops based on L3/L4 match criteria.

pages.title: Firewall
pages.summary: Ze manages nftables packet filter and NAT rules from a single firewall { } YANG section.

pages.title: Traffic Control
pages.summary: Ze programs per-interface queueing disciplines, classes, and filters from a single traffic { control { } } YANG section.

pages.title: Class of Service
pages.summary: Class-of-Service (CoS) in Ze maps the 3-bit IEEE 802.1p Priority Code Point (PCP) in 802.1Q VLAN headers to internal priorities and back.

pages.title: L2TP/PPP
pages.summary: Ze includes a native L2TPv2 (RFC 2661) LNS/LAC implementation for use as a BNG (Broadband Network Gateway) component.

pages.title: PPPoE
pages.summary: Ze implements an RFC 2516 PPPoE access concentrator for direct-attach subscriber access.

pages.title: VPP Data Plane
pages.summary: Ze optionally integrates with VPP (the FD.io Vector Packet Processor) to forward packets at DPDK speed.

pages.title: RPKI
pages.summary: Ze validates received BGP routes against RPKI ROA data.

pages.title: IPsec VPN
pages.summary: Ze implements native IKEv2 in Go for route-based IPsec VPN tunnels.

pages.title: TACACS+ AAA
pages.summary: Ze authenticates SSH logins against TACACS+ servers (RFC 8907) when the system.authentication.tacacs block is present.

pages.title: RADIUS AAA
pages.summary: Ze authenticates operator logins (SSH, web, MCP) against RADIUS servers (RFC 2865) when the system.authentication.radius block is present.

pages.title: AS112 DNS
pages.summary: Ze's as112 plugin runs an AS112 anycast DNS node: an authoritative sink for misdirected reverse-DNS queries about RFC 1918 and link-local address space (RFC 7534), plus the EMPTY.AS112.ARPA...

pages.title: DNS
pages.summary: Ze is on both sides of DNS.

pages.title: Authorization
pages.summary: Ze supports profile-based command authorization.

pages.title: Fleet
pages.summary: Fleet mode is Ze's answer to "I have 20 boxes and I want to manage their config from one place".

pages.title: BGP
pages.summary: The BGP subtree of the config.

pages.title: Peers
pages.summary: A BGP peer in Ze is a named entry under bgp { peer <name> { } }.

pages.title: Policies
pages.summary: Ze does not have a built-in filter language in the style of BIRD's filter DSL or FRR's route-map.

pages.title: Address Families
pages.summary: Address families in Ze fall into two groups.

pages.title: ADD-PATH
pages.summary: ADD-PATH (RFC 7911) lets BGP advertise more than one path per prefix by prefixing each NLRI with a 4-byte Path Identifier.

pages.title: Graceful Restart
pages.summary: Graceful Restart (RFC 4724) and Long-Lived Graceful Restart (RFC 9494) let a BGP session preserve forwarding state across a restart of one side, instead of dropping every route and waiting for...

pages.title: BGP Role
pages.summary: BGP Role (RFC 9234) prevents route leaks by declaring the business relationship between peers.

pages.title: Route Reflection
pages.summary: Ze operates as both a route server (RFC 7947) and an iBGP route reflector (RFC 4456).

pages.title: Route Injection
pages.summary: Route injection is one of the two things Ze was built for.

pages.title: Route Filters
pages.summary: Route filters let plugins act on BGP UPDATEs as they move through the daemon.

pages.title: Operation
pages.summary: This section is for the day-2 operator.

pages.title: Starting and Stopping
pages.summary: Running Ze is the same as running any other Unix daemon with one small twist: SSH credentials must exist before the daemon can expose its CLI.

pages.title: Show Commands
pages.summary: This is the day-2 operator's quick reference for the ze show family.

pages.title: Monitoring
pages.summary: Ze gives you three different ways to watch a running daemon: an auto-refreshing peer dashboard for the operator at the keyboard, a live event stream for the engineer chasing a bug, and a Prometheus...

pages.title: Flow Export
pages.summary: Ze exports interface counters and per-flow records to external collectors over UDP.

pages.title: DDoS Mitigation
pages.summary: Ze can automatically detect volumetric DDoS attacks on its interfaces, mitigate them on the host or upstream, and report incidents to the Flowtriq cloud.

pages.title: Anomaly Detection
pages.summary: Ze has a behavioral anomaly detector: a report-only subsystem that builds a per-source behavioral baseline, scores how far each source deviates from its own history and from its peers, and correlates...

pages.title: Health Checks
pages.summary: Ze provides two complementary systems for monitoring operational health: offline doctor checks (pre-start readiness) and runtime health monitoring (continuous anomaly detection during operation).

pages.title: Audit Trail
pages.summary: Ze keeps a local structured audit log for operator actions that change state or fail authentication.

pages.title: Production Diagnostics
pages.summary: Symptom-based troubleshooting using Ze's built-in diagnostic commands.

pages.title: Logging
pages.summary: Ze uses hierarchical, structured logging with runtime-configurable levels per subsystem.

pages.title: Operational Reports
pages.summary: Ze has a single bus for operator-visible issues, backed by two CLI commands: ze show warnings and ze show errors.

pages.title: Healthcheck
pages.summary: The Ze healthcheck monitors a service by running a shell command on a timer and controls BGP route announcement or withdrawal through a watchdog group.

pages.title: Self-Update
pages.summary: Ze can automatically download, verify, and install firmware updates on non-gokrazy deployments.

pages.title: Zero-Touch Provisioning
pages.summary: ze install remote is a one-command, zero-touch provisioning (ZTP) server that PXE-boots target machines with a gokrazy appliance image containing Ze.

pages.title: MRT Analysis
pages.summary: Ze provides both daemon-side MRT recording and a standalone analysis tool.

pages.title: Upgrade and Restart
pages.summary: The point of this page is one thing: how to replace the binary, reload the config, or restart the daemon without dropping your BGP sessions or black-holing traffic.

pages.title: Interfaces
pages.summary: Ze exposes the same engine through five different surfaces.

pages.title: CLI
pages.summary: The CLI is a network OS shell, not a Unix wrapper.

pages.title: Web UI
pages.summary: The web UI is the same engine as the CLI with a different surface.

pages.title: Looking Glass
pages.summary: The Looking Glass is the public, read-only side of Ze.

pages.title: MCP
pages.summary: The MCP server is the surface you use when an AI assistant should drive Ze.

pages.title: REST API
pages.summary: The REST API is Ze's programmatic HTTP surface for running commands and editing configuration from anywhere that can speak JSON.

pages.title: gRPC API
pages.summary: The gRPC API is the typed-RPC counterpart to the REST API.

pages.title: gNMI
pages.summary: Ze includes a gNMI (gRPC Network Management Interface) server that exposes the YANG-modeled configuration over the industry-standard gNMI protocol.

pages.title: Introspection
pages.summary: Ze is self-documenting.

pages.title: Plugins
pages.summary: A plugin in Ze is a unit of behaviour that registers itself with the engine and reacts to events on the bus.

pages.title: bgp-rib
pages.summary: The main BGP RIB store and best-path selection engine.

pages.title: bgp-adj-rib-in
pages.summary: Per-peer Adj-RIB-In store with raw hex replay for forensic analysis and route server convergence.

pages.title: bgp-persist
pages.summary: In-memory sent-route cache with replay on peer reconnect.

pages.title: bgp-rs
pages.summary: RFC 7947 route server: forwards every received route to every other peer, with zero-copy wire forwarding when peers share an encoding context.

pages.title: bgp-rr
pages.summary: RFC 4456 iBGP route reflector.

pages.title: bgp-filter-community
pages.summary: Community filter plugin for tagging, stripping, and matching communities (standard, large, extended) on ingress and egress.

pages.title: bgp-filter-prefix
pages.summary: Named prefix-list filter (CIDR + ge/le + accept/reject).

pages.title: bgp-filter-aspath
pages.summary: Named AS-path regex filter (ordered entries, first match wins, accept/reject).

pages.title: bgp-route-modify
pages.summary: Named route attribute modifier.

pages.title: bgp-filter-irr
pages.summary: The bgp-filter-irr plugin filters incoming BGP routes against prefix lists derived from Internet Routing Registry (IRR) data.

pages.title: bgp-redistribute
pages.summary: Cross-protocol route redistribution.

pages.title: bgp-role
pages.summary: RFC 9234 BGP Role enforcement.

pages.title: bgp
pages.summary: The core BGP plugin implementing RFC 4271.

pages.title: bgp-healthcheck
pages.summary: Service healthcheck plugin with watchdog route control.

pages.title: interface
pages.summary: OS network interface monitoring and management.

pages.title: loop
pages.summary: Route loop detection ingress filter per RFC 4271 Section 9 and RFC 4456 Section 8.

pages.title: bgp-gr
pages.summary: Graceful Restart (RFC 4724) and Long-Lived Graceful Restart (RFC 9494) state machine.

pages.title: bgp-watchdog
pages.summary: Deferred route announcement controlled by named watchdog groups.

pages.title: bgp-route-refresh
pages.summary: Route Refresh (RFC 2918) and Enhanced Route Refresh (RFC 7313).

pages.title: bgp-rpki
pages.summary: RPKI origin validation via the RTR protocol (RFC 6811, RFC 8210) and ASPA path verification with policy enforcement (RTR v2, RFC 9582, draft-ietf-sidrops-aspa-verification).

pages.title: bgp-rpki-decorator
pages.summary: Correlates UPDATE events and RPKI validation events into merged update-rpki events for consumer plugins that want both in one envelope.

pages.title: bgp-aigp
pages.summary: Accumulated IGP metric (RFC 7311).

pages.title: bgp-hostname
pages.summary: FQDN capability. Advertises the local hostname and fully-qualified domain name to peers in the OPEN message.

pages.title: bgp-llnh
pages.summary: Link-Local Next Hop for IPv6 (RFC 2545).

pages.title: bgp-softver
pages.summary: Software version capability.

pages.title: bgp-nlri-vpn
pages.summary: MPLS-VPN address families: IPv4 VPN (AFI 1 / SAFI 128) and IPv6 VPN (AFI 2 / SAFI 128), per RFC 4364.

pages.title: bgp-nlri-evpn
pages.summary: L2VPN EVPN (AFI 25 / SAFI 70), per RFC 7432.

pages.title: bgp-nlri-flowspec
pages.summary: BGP FlowSpec (RFC 8955, RFC 8956) for IPv4 and IPv6, plus the VPN variants.

pages.title: bgp-nlri-ls
pages.summary: BGP Link-State (RFC 7752) and its VPN variant.

pages.title: bgp-nlri-labeled
pages.summary: MPLS labelled unicast for IPv4 (AFI 1 / SAFI 4) and IPv6 (AFI 2 / SAFI 4).

pages.title: bgp-nlri-vpls
pages.summary: L2VPN VPLS (AFI 25 / SAFI 65), RFC 4761 / RFC 4762.

pages.title: bgp-nlri-mvpn
pages.summary: Multicast VPN (RFC 6513, RFC 6514) for IPv4 (AFI 1 / SAFI 5) and IPv6 (AFI 2 / SAFI 5).

pages.title: bgp-nlri-rtc
pages.summary: Route Target Constrain (RFC 4684).

pages.title: bgp-nlri-mup
pages.summary: Mobile User Plane SAFI for IPv4 (AFI 1 / SAFI 85) and IPv6 (AFI 2 / SAFI 85).

pages.title: bgp-nlri-srpolicy
pages.summary: SR-Policy NLRI (SAFI 73, RFC 9830) carries Segment Routing policy information over BGP.

pages.title: bgp-bmp
pages.summary: Ze implements RFC 7854 BMP in both directions: as a receiver (accepting feeds from routers) and as a sender (streaming state to collectors).

pages.title: ntp
pages.summary: Ze includes an NTP client plugin for system clock synchronization.

pages.title: sysctl
pages.summary: Ze includes a sysctl plugin that manages kernel parameters with named profiles.

pages.title: dhcp-server
pages.summary: DHCP server plugin serving leases to LAN clients per RFC 2131/2132.

pages.title: fib-kernel
pages.summary: Programs the Linux kernel forwarding table via netlink.

pages.title: fib-p4
pages.summary: Experimental P4 dataplane backend.

pages.title: iface-dhcp
pages.summary: DHCP client for managed interfaces.

pages.title: iface-netlink
pages.summary: Netlink backend for the iface component.

pages.title: sysrib
pages.summary: Cross-protocol RIB selector.

pages.title: host
pages.summary: The host inventory plugin provides hardware detection, SMART health monitoring, and a hardware tuning engine.

pages.summary: This page is the five-minute version of writing a Go plugin against the Ze SDK.

pages.title: External Plugins
pages.summary: An external plugin is a separate process.

pages.title: YANG Schema
pages.summary: Every plugin that has its own configuration ships a YANG schema.

pages.title: Handlers
pages.summary: Handlers are the callbacks a plugin registers with the SDK to react to engine-initiated events.

pages.title: Commands
pages.summary: A plugin exposes commands by declaring them in its Registration at startup and handling them with OnExecuteCommand at runtime.

pages.title: Testing
pages.summary: The Ze plugin SDK is designed to be testable.

pages.title: Chaos Testing
pages.summary: Chaos testing is built into Ze.

pages.title: Dashboard
pages.summary: The chaos dashboard is a live web UI for ze-chaos.

pages.title: Property Verification
pages.summary: Property verification is the part of ze-chaos that turns "did the run finish without crashing" into something useful.

pages.title: Blueprints
pages.summary: Blueprints are end-to-end worked examples.

pages.title: Route Server at an IXP
pages.summary: Running Ze as an IXP route server.

pages.title: Transit Edge with RPKI
pages.summary: A transit customer edge router.

pages.title: Public Looking Glass
pages.summary: Stand up a public Looking Glass for your AS.

pages.title: ExaBGP Migration Walkthrough
pages.summary: A complete worked migration of a non-trivial ExaBGP setup to Ze.

pages.title: FlowSpec Injection
pages.summary: Inject BGP FlowSpec rules from a script for DDoS mitigation.

pages.title: Chaos-Tested Peering
pages.summary: Set up a peering session and verify that it survives a battery of chaos scenarios.

pages.title: AS Path Topology
pages.summary: Use the Looking Glass topology graph to visualise a real network's AS paths.

pages.title: Development
pages.summary: This is the developer's section.

pages.title: Building
pages.summary: Building Ze from source is a single command if you have Go 1.26 and a working toolchain on the path.

pages.title: Repo Layout
pages.summary: The Ze repo is organised around three top-level Go directories (cmd/, internal/, pkg/) and a set of supporting directories for docs, tests, schemas, and tooling.

pages.title: Coding Standards
pages.summary: Ze has a set of coding rules that apply to every contribution, whether you write the code by hand or with AI assistance.

pages.title: Testing
pages.summary: Ze has five test suites: unit, functional, fuzz, chaos, and mutation.

pages.title: Debugging
pages.summary: Debugging Ze is mostly a matter of knowing which tool to reach for.

pages.title: CI
pages.summary: Ze's CI runs the same Make targets that you run locally, so that "works locally" and "passes CI" are the same statement.

pages.title: RFC Compliance
pages.summary: Ze implements a lot of standards documents.

pages.title: Contributing
pages.summary: Contributions to Ze are welcome.

pages.title: Claude Code
pages.summary: Ze is developed with Claude Code, and the repo ships a set of project-specific slash commands under .claude/skills/.

pages.title: Performance
pages.summary: ze-perf is a BGP propagation latency benchmark tool.

pages.title: Mock Servers
pages.summary: ze-test is the test harness for Ze.

pages.summary: The reference section is where you look when you need an exact answer.

pages.summary: Ze commands fall into two categories.
